name: API - Nearshore Small Balance Open Card

1.content:
Small Balance Cards are those with remaining balances of $10 or less. You will identify the source of those funds, and ensure all funds are reabsorbed by Corpay, refunded to the Client, or reissued to the Vendor as appropriate.

Open the Nearshore Small Balance Followup Sheet and locate the section labeled with your name. Each row in the spreadsheet contains the information about one card that has an open balance. You should work cards in order, based on the following criteria:

  • Work all cards that do NOT have the word "Fee" in the Fee column, from oldest to newest.*
  • Work cases that have the word "Fee" in the Fee column, from oldest to newest.

*Small balance cards labeled "fee" are much more likely to have a remaining balance from a fee that Corpay paid, rather than leftover funding from the customer. We want to prioritize getting our customer's money back to them first!

Locate the next card to be worked based on the criteria above, and copy the Payment ID for that card.

9.notes:
Logic explanation:
funding==remaining_balance
(funding+fee_amount)==remaining_balance
If the funding amount matches the amount on the card, or funding + fee equals the amount remaining on the card, that means the card was never run at all and needs completely cancelled and reissued.

fee_amount==remaining_balance
manual_load_value==remaining_balance
If the fee is exactly equal to the remainder, or the amount manually added by Corpay (generally to cover a fee) is equal to the remainder, we assume the remaining amount is unused fee funds and cancel them back to ourselves.

remaining_balance>1
client_exception=='Yes'
If the card has over a dollar on it, or the Client REALLY wants every cent back that might be theirs, we initiate a partial refund to give the client back whatever was left on the card.

And the 'fail state' is cards under $1 that don't meet any other criteria - those are assumed to be bits of leftover fees and canceled back to Corpay.

10.content:
The remainder on the card indicates that this card was never processed, and should be cancelled and reissued as a check.

Create a new note in the Payment Notes section of the Payment Details page in Bizpay with the format:
MM/DD/YY Pmt never processed, CANCEL/ISSUE CHECK $#remaining_balance# - [INITIALS]

Once you have typed the payment note into the "Add New Note Here" field, click Save.

11.content:
This card has a remainder of less than $1, which is likely left over from fees and needs cancelled.

Create a new note in the Payment Notes section of the Payment Details page in Bizpay with the format:
MM/DD/YY vendor processed partial payment, $1 or less remaining, CANCEL FEE $#remaining_balance#  - [INITIALS]

Once you have typed the payment note into the "Add New Note Here" field, click Save.

12.content:
The remainder matches the fee/amount manually added to the card, so it is Corpay's load to cover a fee. You will cancel the fee to recoup the remainder.

Create a new note in the Payment Notes section of the Payment Details page in Bizpay with the format:
MM/DD/YY fee not needed CANCEL FEE $#remaining_balance# - [INITIALS]

Once you have typed the payment note into the "Add New Note Here" field, click Save.

13.content:
There is a significant remaining balance on the card that likely came from client funding, so you will initiate a partial refund.

Create a new note in the Payment Notes section of the Payment Details page in Bizpay with the format:
MM/DD/YY vendor processed partial payment, CANCEL/PARTIAL REFUND $#remaining_balance# - [INITIALS]

Once you have typed the payment note into the "Add New Note Here" field, click Save.

14.content:
Initiate Cancel Card within Bizpay.

  • Recommended Action: Fee
  • Cancel Reason: Fee not needed
  • Amount to Cancel: #remaining_balance# 
  • Fee: #remaining_balance#

Read More: How to Initiate Cancel Card▼

  1. From the Payment Details page in Bizpay, click the Actions button and select Initiate Cancel Card.
  2. An Initiate Cancel Card Request window will open. Take the following actions:
    A: Recommended Action – Select Fee.
    B: Amount – Key in the remaining balance of the card, #remaining_balance#.
    C: Cancel Reason – Select Fee not needed. (This option is automatically selected.)
    D: Fee – Key in the remaining balance of the card, #remaining_balance#.
    E: Payment Notes – This field will prepopulate; do not update it.
    F: Payment Completion Notes – This field will prepopulate; do not update it.
    G: Click Submit.

25.content:
Open the Card Details page in Galileo, and navigate to the All Transactions section. Review all transactions listed in this section, comparing them to what you see in Bizpay's Settlement History.

Read More: Researching a Card in Galileo▼

  1. Log in to Galileo. On the dashboard that populates, click CST to open the Galileo Customer Service Tool.
  2. Under the Account tab, select External Account ID from the drop-down. Then, paste the Payment ID (from either the Follow Up Spreadsheet or Bizpay) into the field and click Search.
  3. Click on either one of the linked numbers in the Card Number/PRN column to open the Card Details.
  4. Expand the Account Info section and select All Transactions.
  5. If needed, adjust the Start Date to view all transactions processed on the card, and click Submit to update the results. The default display shows transactions processed in the last 30 days; it is recommended to use the transaction date associated with the Funding transaction in Bizpay as the Start Date.

37.content:
The remainder on the card indicates that this card was never processed, and should be cancelled and reissued via RPPS.

Create a new note in the Payment Notes section of the Payment Details page in Bizpay with the format:

38.content:

41.content:
Review the Client Notes field carefully and thoroughly to determine whether the Client has any restrictions relating to partial refunds (or refunds in general).

A Client may not allow any partial refunds or may have required approval steps before a partial refund can be processed. If either scenario applies, select Yes below.

Read More: How to Review Client Notes▼

1. Move your cursor over the hyperlinked Client Nameat the top of the Payment Details page and review the Notes field that populates. If the Notes do not display correctly or you are unable to review the full contents of the field, continue to the next step. 

2. Click the hyperlinked Client Name to navigate to the Client Details page. Scroll down the page to locate the Notes section, then review the information.
